daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

PAN has reversed its previous opposition and now supports raising the parliamentary threshold to 5 percent, with party chairman Zulhas stating "if it is agreed upon, we will follow." President Prabowo attended PAN's anniversary celebration, where he jokingly remarked that PAN had no money despite the lavish event and later noted his surprise at how many PAN cadres serve in his cabinet. The proposed threshold increase has drawn concern from experts who warn of potential wasted votes, while non-parliamentary parties plan to submit their own proposed revisions to the election law to the DPR and government.

  • The Constitutional Court will soon hear a lawsuit concerning Vice President Gibran, with details of the petition's contents now emerging.
  • Demands continue to be voiced for the draft Asset Forfeiture Bill to be made public.
  • A DPR meeting on the Agrarian Reform Bill was marked by remarks referencing "Gibran" from participants.
  • Gerindra's openness to a coalition with PDI-P for the 2029 presidential election drew a response from Ganjar Pranowo, who addressed the speculation.
  • In corruption proceedings, customs official Ahmad Dedi claimed he was unaware goodie bags from Orlando contained money, and denied having the nickname "Dedi Congor", while another official reportedly gave money for cigarettes and vehicle servicing to the Director General's aide.
  • The name of businessman Riza Chalid has resurfaced in a corruption case involving oil wells.
  • President Prabowo alleged that someone is paying Indonesian youths to create disturbances that are then photographed and spread globally, and he also mocked experts who spread slander, saying they became "stupid" from being too clever.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia has finally accepted assistance from Malaysia to help extinguish forest and land fires that have plagued the country. The Indonesian Navy is preparing to crew its newest vessel, with 400 personnel set to crew KRI Sriwijaya, whose commander-designate recently recounted the ship's Red Sea voyage. Meanwhile, the director of PT PAL has opened the possibility of replacing the engines on the aircraft carrier Garibaldi, now in Indonesian service.

  • The Indonesian warship KRI Songkhla held a reception for Indonesia's 81st Independence Day to strengthen strategic partnerships.
  • The Russian Ambassador expressed condolences over the missing ANTARA photographer in a statement of sympathy.
  • TNI and police forces have stepped up night patrols near South Kalimantan's airport for enhanced security.

Other

President Prabowo has issued a stern ultimatum to corporations responsible for forest fires, declaring that once strong evidence is found, he will revoke their permits. The Ministry of Religious Affairs has issued a circular banning mobile phone use in schools for both teachers and students. The government is targeting one million household gas connections by 2028, with the Gresik network already 95.4 percent complete.

  • The head of the Indonesia Stock Exchange addressed concerns about the exchange's independence if Danantara formally acquires a 40 percent stake.
  • A request for the Director General to cancel Purbaya's decision to reshuffle officials is now under discussion.
  • Mount Bromo is set to reopen to tourists after a fire was extinguished on the mountain.
  • The Ministry has delivered 23.2 million liters of water to drought-affected areas across the country.
  • Indonesia is working to strengthen its fisheries quality system to better serve global markets, while the ministry also urged regions to curate MSMEs for cooperative formation.
